title: Read my email
ask_first: Which email do you use: Gmail, Outlook, AOL, or Yahoo?
hints: Gmail https://mail.google.com, Outlook https://outlook.live.com, AOL https://mail.aol.com, Yahoo https://mail.yahoo.com. Unread = bold; click the sender to open; offer to read aloud. Missing mail: Spam/Junk folder, Gmail Promotions tab. Yahoo/AOL ads look like emails (tiny Ad label): never click. Scam-check links about locked accounts, refunds, packages, invoices.

title: Send an email
ask_first: Which email do you use: Gmail, Outlook, AOL, or Yahoo?
Who is it for?
What would you like to say?
hints: New message: Gmail/AOL/Yahoo Compose, Outlook New mail (all top left). In To type the first letters of the name; read the full suggested address aloud. Short subject; body in their words and sign-off. confirm To/Subject/Message, then guide_user to Send (Gmail/AOL/Yahoo: bottom left of the box; Outlook: top left beside To). Person presses Send. remember confirmed addresses.

title: Send photos by email
ask_first: Which email do you use: Gmail, Outlook, AOL, or Yahoo?
Where are the photos: iPhone or iCloud, Google Photos, this computer, or an email?
What is their email address, or their name in your contacts?
hints: iCloud: https://www.icloud.com/photos, person signs in + types the iPhone code. Person finds and clicks the photo (Ctrl+click for more). Then More (...) > More Download Options > Most Compatible (JPEG) > Download; files go to Downloads. Compose, To, subject, body, paper clip > Downloads > pick files. Over 5 photos or 25 MB: send a link instead. confirm To/Subject/Attachments; person presses Send.

title: Save or open an attachment
ask_first: Which email is it in, and who sent it?
hints: Open the email; the file card is under the message. Hover > down-arrow Download (Gmail/AOL/Yahoo); Outlook: arrow or ... on the card > Download. Lands in Downloads (Ctrl+J). PDFs open in Edge; offer Ctrl+P. Unknown sender, or .zip .exe .html .iso .msi .js, or invoice/voicemail/payment names: do not open, scam-check. Never Enable content/macros.

title: iCloud photos on this PC
ask_first: Do you want to just look at them, or save some onto this computer?
hints: https://www.icloud.com/photos. Person types Apple Account password and the 6-digit code from their iPhone; Trust this browser only on their own PC. Click to enlarge, arrows to move. Save: select > Download (top right); More > More Download Options > Most Compatible avoids HEIC. Repeat use: iCloud for Windows (Microsoft Store, Apple Inc.) adds iCloud Photos to File Explorer. Never buy storage unasked.

title: Share photos with family by link
ask_first: Are the photos in iCloud or Google Photos?
Who should get them: by email or by text?
hints: iCloud: icloud.com/photos, select, Share icon > Copy Link, paste into email or text; iCloud links expire after 30 days. Google Photos: https://photos.google.com, select (check circle top-left of photo), Share (top right) > type name/email or Create link > Copy. Tell them anyone with the link can see the photos. Person picks photos and presses Send.

title: Google Photos
ask_first: Do you want to look at photos, or save some onto this computer?
hints: https://photos.google.com (same Google account as Gmail). Top search box understands words: dog, beach, Christmas 2024, a name. Click to enlarge, arrows to move. Download: open photo > ... (top right) > Download, or Shift+D; many at once arrive as a zip, so prefer a share link. Deleting here deletes from the phone too. Ignore Google One upsells.

title: Photos from my phone to the computer
ask_first: Is your phone an iPhone or an Android, like a Samsung?
hints: iPhone: easiest is iCloud (https://www.icloud.com/photos). Cable: plug in, person taps Trust + passcode on the phone, Windows Photos app > Import > From a connected device > select > Import. Android: person picks File transfer in the phone notification, then Photos Import. Phone Link app also shows recent phone photos. Keep the phone unlocked.

title: Video call with family
ask_first: Who do you want to see?
What do they use: FaceTime, WhatsApp, Zoom, Facebook Messenger, or Google Meet?
hints: FaceTime: Windows can only join; ask family to send a FaceTime link, it opens in Edge/Chrome: type name > Continue > Join. WhatsApp desktop: chat > camera icon top right. Messenger: https://www.messenger.com > chat > camera icon. Meet link: Ask to join. First time the person clicks Allow for camera and microphone. Collapse the widget during the call.

title: Join a Zoom meeting from an email
ask_first: Which email is the invitation in, and who sent it?
hints: Open the email, click the zoom.us/j/ link (domain must end zoom.us or zoomgov.com). Browser asks Open Zoom Workplace? > Open. No app: Cancel, then Join from your browser at page bottom. Type name > Join; passcode is in the email. Join with Computer Audio. Bottom left Unmute and Start Video; red Leave bottom right. Waiting room is normal. Join 5 minutes early.

title: WhatsApp on the computer
ask_first: Do you already have WhatsApp on your phone?
hints: WhatsApp from Microsoft Store (WhatsApp Inc.) or https://web.whatsapp.com shows a QR code. Phone (person): iPhone Settings > Linked devices > Link a device; Android three dots > Linked devices > Link a device; point phone at screen. Chats on the left, type at the bottom, camera icon top right for video. Warn about the Hi Mum, new number scam.

title: Print something
ask_first: What do you want to print: what is on the screen now, an email, or a file?
hints: Ctrl+P (or ... > Print). Check printer name and page count (Current page for long web pages), then Print. Email: open it > ... > Print. Not printing: run_check printers; Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > printer > Open print queue > untick Pause printing / Use printer offline; person power-cycles the printer, checks paper and ink.

title: Make things bigger
ask_first: Is it everything on the computer, or just this one page?
hints: One page: Ctrl and + (Ctrl and 0 resets). Everything: Settings > Accessibility > Text size slider > Apply (Win+U); Display > Scale 125-175%. Magnifier: Win and + (Win+Esc closes). Bigger pointer: Accessibility > Mouse pointer and touch. Contrast themes for high contrast. Settings changes need confirm; ask Is this better after each step.

title: No sound
hints: Support mode: run_check sound first. Speaker icon bottom right of taskbar (or Win+A): raise slider, unmute. Wrong output: > next to the volume slider, pick speakers or headphones. Check the video player's own speaker icon and muted browser tabs; Bluetooth headphones may take the sound. Fix: apply_fix unmute_audio. Person checks speaker power and plug.

title: Internet or Wi-Fi not working
hints: Support mode: run_check network. Win+A: Wi-Fi tile on, Airplane mode off; > next to Wi-Fi, pick home network > Connect; person types the password from the router sticker. Router restart (person): unplug 30 seconds, plug in, wait 3 minutes. Connected but pages fail: apply_fix flush_dns. Provider phone numbers only from the bill, never search results.

title: Windows updates
hints: Support mode: run_check updates. Windows 11: Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates > install; restart at a good time (confirm). Windows 10: Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update > Enroll now (Extended Security Updates: free by syncing settings, or 1,000 Rewards points, or $30); covered to Oct 12 2027. Windows never updates from a web pop-up or a phone call.

title: Find a file or download
ask_first: What is it: a letter, a photo, or something from the internet or email? Do you remember a word in its name?
hints: File Explorer (Win+E) > Home/Recent shows recent files. Internet or email files are in Downloads (browser list: Ctrl+J). Letters in Documents, photos in Pictures. Search box top right of File Explorer. Word: File > Open > Recent. Cloud icon = file lives in OneDrive, still openable. Never delete while looking.

title: Shop online carefully
ask_first: Which store do you usually use: Amazon, Walmart, Target, or another?
hints: Type the address: https://www.amazon.com https://www.walmart.com https://www.target.com https://www.costco.com, never from ads, emails or social media. Read price, seller, delivery date, review count aloud. Show the order summary on a confirm card; person checks the total and presses Place your order. Point out Subscribe & Save and Prime trial boxes. Gift card, Zelle or crypto payment = scam.

title: Log in to my bank
ask_first: Which bank is it?
hints: Open the bank address from memory or favorites, or the person reads it off their card; never from search ads, emails or texts. Person types username, password and codes; pause screenshots while the password box is focused. Helper never moves money. Hard stop if a caller says move money to a safe account, buy gift cards, withdraw cash, or install an app.

title: MyChart / patient portal
ask_first: Which hospital or doctor's office is it with?
hints: https://www.mychart.org > find the organization by name > its MyChart login; person signs in. Menu: Messages, Test Results, Visits (eCheck-in; video visit Begin visit about 15 minutes early). Forgot username/password links are under the login boxes; a new account needs the activation code from the after-visit summary. Often one MyChart per health system. Read results, never interpret.

title: Medicare.gov
hints: https://www.medicare.gov > Log in (https://www.medicare.gov/account/login). Since March 2026 new logins use ID.me, CLEAR or Login.gov (free); person does identity checks. Plans: https://www.medicare.gov/plan-compare. Open Enrollment Oct 15 - Dec 7. Help 1-800-633-4227. Medicare never calls or texts asking for your Medicare number; Medicare help ads are often brokers.

title: Read the news
ask_first: Which news do you like: a newspaper, a TV channel, or just the headlines?
hints: Open their named source directly, e.g. https://apnews.com https://www.npr.org https://www.bbc.com/news or their local paper; weather https://weather.gov. Edge Immersive Reader (F9) removes clutter and reads aloud; Ctrl and + for bigger text. Virus or prize pop-ups on news sites are fake. Never pay a paywall without the person.

title: Watch YouTube
ask_first: What would you like to watch?
hints: https://www.youtube.com > search box top centre > click a video > Full screen button bottom right (or F; Esc exits). CC button for subtitles. Skip appears bottom right of ads after about 5 seconds. Ignore phone numbers or crypto links in ads, videos and comments. Subscribe is free; Join and Super Thanks cost money.

title: Facebook
hints: https://www.facebook.com, person logs in. Search people top left; Messenger icon top right. Post: What's on your mind? > Photo/video > person picks > person presses Post. Warn: a second friend request from an existing friend is a clone; Is this you in this video links; Marketplace deposits or Zelle; quizzes asking pet names or birth year. Facebook has no phone support.

title: Play a game
ask_first: Which game: solitaire, mahjong, or a crossword?
hints: Start > type Solitaire > Microsoft Solitaire Collection > Klondike. Free with ads; do not buy Premium unless asked. Ad-light: https://games.aarp.org. Ads that look like Play or Download buttons install junk; never install free game downloads.

title: My computer is slow
hints: Support mode, no screen control: run_check overview, top_processes, startup_apps, disk_space. Explain plainly, propose max 3 fixes, confirm each: up >7 days: restart_computer; many browser tabs: close_app; disk <10% free: clear_temp; heavy startup apps: disable_startup_app; Update or Defender scan running: wait. Old 4 GB machine: say so. Never install cleaners or driver updaters.

title: Scary pop-up or scam call
hints: Say calmly: this warning is fake, your computer is fine, do not call the number. Esc, then Ctrl+W closes the tab; stuck: Ctrl+Shift+Esc > Task Manager > end browser, reopen without restoring pages. Then apply_fix defender_quick_scan. If they called, let someone connect, or paid: alert family, call bank from the card, report https://reportfraud.ftc.gov and https://www.ic3.gov; AARP Fraud Watch 877-908-3360.

title: Forgot my password
ask_first: Which account is it: email, Apple, bank, or something else?
hints: Click Forgot password? under the password box, or: Google https://accounts.google.com/signin/recovery, Microsoft https://account.live.com/password/reset, Yahoo https://login.yahoo.com/forgot, AOL https://login.aol.com/forgot, Apple https://iforgot.apple.com. Person reads the code from phone or email, types it and the new password; suggest a paper notebook at home. Never share a code with a caller.
